newsitem.title: Singapore: Asia crude steady, China buys heavy Asian grades.
newsitem.headline: Asia crude steady, China buys heavy Asian grades.

text.p: The Asian crude market was active on Monday, with China emerging to buy July Minas crude.
Two July parcels were heard traded to China by two shosha.
The deals were noT confirmed, but levels were heard to be ICP +15, and ICP +20.
A Minas parcel sold by a western trader at just under ICP +20 last week was now heard to have been to an Indonesian affiliate.
Traders were surprised that the affiliate was buying Minas, rather than selling, but thought that it was due to the reduced July allocation volume released by Indonesia.
A 200,000-barrel parcel of July Widuri was also heard done between a shosha and a South Korean refiner at ICP +21.
But the trade could not be confirmed and may have been done more than a week ago, traders said.
The Middle East crude market was quiet, but sentiment for August was bearish, with ample supplies expected to be available, traders said.
Some traders said there was a chance August could see a turnaround in prices when trading starts fully next week, since refiners would have come out of their maintenance shutdowns by then.
But there was concern about refinery margins as product prices were under pressure, which could lead to further refinery run cuts in Asia, they said.
A major was heard to have sold an August Oman at Dubai +25 to a Korean refiner, in exchange for a Dubai cargo at whole month quotes +5. But the major would not comment on the trade.
Oman outright offers were heard coming from MPM -15/-20 for August. But discussion on the Abu Dhabi crudes remained thin as sellers wait for a price indication from buyers.
